item.title: Random thoughts after rewatching Apothecary Diaries Season 1 Episode 3
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I rewatched Apothecary Diaries season 1 episode 3 twice. 7/10.

This was a sleepwalking lady's story. OK, I didn't notice at first, but Jinshi got a letter from the military officer, so he suspected Concubine Fuyou had lied. And that was the reason he wasn't convinced by Maomao's suggestion. So, he wanted to make sure and tried to work out what kind of person Maomao was.

Also, Maomao started wondering who the hell he was. Of course, she was smart, and he freely walked around the rear palace, so that was very natural. Her conjecture was also somewhat true. He was definitely the Emperor's favorite. She also knew a lot of people and cases in the Verdigris House and remembered them. She was curious about everything but gossip.

But why was Lady Gyokuyou envious of Concubine Fuyou? Didn't she have someone she wanted to be with, even though she was with the Emperor? Maybe it was a lot of pressure to be one of the Emperor's concubines.

It was good that the quack doctor had already forgiven Maomao as well. He might've been afraid of someone who didn't know medicines touching anything in his storeroom.

And then, why was there another song in this episode when Concubine Fuyou met the military officer? Was she actually an important person?

item.title: Random thoughts after rewatching Apothecary Diaries Season 1 Episode 2
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I rewatched Apothecary Diaries season 1 episode 2 twice. 6/10.

Maomao was too smart when she figured out the issue. Honestly, there could've been a lot of reasons why people could've been poisoned, not only the smoke from the firewood. Or maybe actually not? It actually sounds weird that many people fell ill after they ate something, so the poison must have spread easily, and it must have happened while or right after they ate dinner at the camp. Also, they had nausea and other symptoms that were able to help her figure it out. And it happened at night, so that might've been another reason why she was able to figure it out. Well, she said it was just her own opinion.

Her co-workers also sympathized with her and were interested in her. She didn't understand how other people saw her. Though, how did other people communicate with her before she ended up in the rear palace? Maybe they didn't care about her at all, and they didn't notice the bandages on her left arm. Or they were already her friends and they knew she liked experiments a lot. So she might actually know how other people saw her.

She also knew what was expensive and what was important. Probably the rear palace was the best place to get medicinal ingredients. And she always figured out what each ingredient was, and how expensive paper was.

I knew who Jinshi was, but from this episode, at least we knew Jinshi was high-ranking in the palace hierarchy. He was able to find and collect precious ingredients from the medicine storehouse, and he was also given a task by the emperor to test the other women's loyalty. That made me realize why he was interested in Maomao. Sure she was unique among women. Why didn't Maomao realize how high-ranking he was, though he talked with Gyokuyou in a friendly way, and frequently? Maybe she thought he was just one of Gyokuyou's favorites?

In the first place, what is the era of this world? At least they have cacao in the rear palace, but I have no idea when it reached East Asia.

In terms of animation, they used lighting pretty well when Maomao first saw the storeroom for medicine ingredients. She stood in a dark room, but it lit up, and then the scene added some visual effects.

item.title: Random thoughts after rewatching Apothecary Diaries Season 1 Episode 1
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I rewatched Apothecary Diaries season 1 episode 1 twice. 7/10. I watched it until the middle of season 2, but this was a complex story so I wanted to start again from the beginning and understand it better.

First of all, the voice actress for Maomao, Aoi Yuki, was so good. How she speaks changes so much with her emotions, even in normal scenes. It showed Maomao's character, too.

In terms of the story, it's still a bit of a mystery why Maomao ended up living in the rear palace after being abducted. Maybe a later episode explains it, but I forgot what it was.

Also, episode 1 showed pretty well what this series was, or who Maomao was. She was a curious cat, who didn't want to get involved in anything terrible like the rear palace or concubines at all. Also, the story misled me about her character a little when she showed she had a complex about her face and her body.

Jinshi already showed he was a person who liked to scheme and worked pretty well, and he was smart as hell. His voice was also so good.

Well, there's nothing else on my mind. As I saw the first time, the backgrounds are absolutely gorgeous, and the clothes and characters are colorful and varied.
